reply.answer: Concentration in AI backlog is extreme for the pure-play infrastructure providers. CoreWeave's ~$103.7 billion RPO is dominated by a handful of names: OpenAI (~$6.5 billion contracted through 2031) and Meta (~$21 billion committed through 2032), with the company itself warning that customer concentration with a limited number of top clients will likely persist. IREN similarly derives a large portion of its AI Cloud Services revenue from a small number of customers, highlighted by its five-year Microsoft agreement announced November 2025 covering GPU acquisitions and 'Horizon' capacity builds. Alphabet's revenue backlog includes $16.8 billion tied to a single related-party joint venture (Crux AI), and Amazon's AWS backlog growth is explicitly driven by two counterparties—OpenAI (~$138 billion cumulative) and Anthropic (>$100 billion expansion)—rather than a broad customer base. TeraWulf's new HPC lease backlog is anchored by Fluidstack and Anthropic. In aggregate, the disclosed RPO/backlog growth across CoreWeave, IREN, Alphabet, Amazon, and TeraWulf in 2025-2026 is attributable overwhelmingly to a small handful of AI labs/hyperscalers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft), meaning backlog quality is highly dependent on the credit and continued scaling plans of just 3-4 counterparties.
reply.next_question: What server and network useful lives do these companies assume, and what is the earnings effect if GPUs/chips last only 3-4 years instead of 6, given how much of the hyperscalers' backlog and capex (e.g., Oracle's $664B RPO against $47B OCF) rests on long depreciation schedules supporting thin near-term margins?
